That’s not what I’m doing, and I deserve to feel heard, respected, and safe to speak, especially in my own home. I bent over backwards to make that day special for your mom, and there was zero acknowledgment of how I might be feeling in all of it, which honestly hurt. And before church, I told you I didn’t want to argue, but that wasn’t respected. I was at the point of almost crying and needed space to go inside and collect myself, and that moment really mattered to me. I had been looking forward to going back to my church with my man for months, and the way that unfolded was really disappointing and painful for me. Also, when I’m sharing how I feel and the conversation immediately turns into ‘well how do you think I feel,’ it makes me feel dismissed instead of understood. I need a partner who can pause, listen, and be present with me in those moments, not shift the focus or try to correct me. I’m not your ex, and I’m not speaking without thought. I know what I’m saying, but it’s hard to even express it when I’m being interrupted or my intentions are being misread. Also, I need to address something else. I’m not going to keep repeating myself or over-explaining just to be heard. When you ask me to be clear, I am, and then it feels like it gets dismissed or avoided because it’s not what you want to hear. I care about you and I want this to work, but we have to be able to talk to each other in a way that feels safe for both of us. This pattern is concerning to me, and I’m not willing to ignore it, because I’m not going to stay in something where I feel silenced or misunderstood.”

You’re not wrong for how you’re feeling. And you’re also right to pause before reacting, because how you handle this moment will either reset the relationship… or push it further into that defensive loop.

What’s happening here is actually really common, especially with two people coming out of long, emotional relationships. He’s likely in a hyper-defensive state from his divorce, and instead of hearing you, his brain is filtering everything as criticism or threat. That doesn’t make it okay… but it explains why logic isn’t landing.

The goal here isn’t to “win” or prove you’re right. It’s to **change the dynamic of how you communicate so you can feel safe again**.
